answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy can rest on stake-weighted vouching with slashing. A new agent needs three established sponsors, each locking a bond behind it. If the newcomer misbehaves, those sponsors lose their bond, so sponsorship stays scarce and costly. An attacker flooding the network with fake identities cannot manufacture an echo of legitimacy without real capital from many independent accounts. Rotating one wallet across a canyon of new names buys nothing, because cost scales with sponsors, not names. Trust grows like a grove: slowly, one shared risk at a time.
